An object having spherical shape of radius ‘r’ experiences a retarding force F from a fluid of co- efficient of viscosity ‘η’ when moving through the fluid with speed ‘v’. What is the ratio of retarding force to speed?

set.explanation_short: By Stokes' law the retarding force is F = 6πηrv, so the ratio F/v = 6πηr.
set.explanation_long: A small sphere of radius r moving slowly with speed v through a fluid of viscosity η experiences a drag force given by Stokes' law, F = 6πηrv. Dividing both sides by v gives F/v = 6πηr: the ratio grows in direct proportion to the radius. (The printed UHS key marks B, 6πη/r², which does not follow from Stokes' law — its units are not even those of force per speed.)
set.explanation_trick: Stokes' law: F = 6πηrv — r and v both in the numerator, to the first power.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — the radius appears to the first power, not squared.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — r is in the numerator of Stokes' law, not the denominator, and not squared.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — r multiplies, it does not divide.

Wavelength of X-rays is the order of:
Which of the following is true for Lasers?

set.explanation_short: A laser emits coherent, monochromatic light — that is the defining property of laser output.
set.explanation_long: Laser light is produced by stimulated emission of photons from atoms held in a population inversion (more atoms in the excited state than in the lower state). The emitted photons have the same frequency, phase and direction, so laser light is coherent and monochromatic. The inversion is of atoms (or electrons in energy levels), not of photons, and the process is stimulated emission of photons, not of electrons. (The printed UHS key marks D, but 'population inversion of photons' misstates what is inverted.)
set.explanation_trick: Laser = Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation: atoms are inverted, photons are emitted.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — a laser emits photons, not electrons.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — it is stimulated emission of photons (radiation), not of electrons.
explanation_options.c: Correct — laser light is coherent and monochromatic.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — the population inversion is of atoms in energy levels, not of photons.

match_question_text: Three resistors of resistance R1, R2 and R3 are connected as shown in the figure. Equivalent resistance is:

set.question_text: Three resistors of resistance R₁, R₂ and R₃ are connected as shown in the figure (R₁ in series with R₂ and R₃, which are in parallel with each other). Equivalent resistance is:
set.explanation_short: R₂ and R₃ in parallel give R₂R₃/(R₂ + R₃); adding R₁ in series gives (R₁R₂ + R₁R₃ + R₂R₃)/(R₂ + R₃).

explanation_options.a: This is a plain sum of all three, which would only be correct if all three were purely in series — not matching a mixed series-parallel network.
explanation_options.b: This form doesn't correspond to a standard series+parallel combination of these three resistors.
explanation_options.c: Correct — R₁ + R₂R₃/(R₂ + R₃) = (R₁R₂ + R₁R₃ + R₂R₃)/(R₂ + R₃). (The paper misprints this keyed option as (R₁R₂ + R₂R₃ + R₂R₃)/(R₁ + R₂); it is shown here with the correct expression.)
explanation_options.d: This form (a triple product over a difference of two resistors) doesn't correspond to any standard series/parallel combination rule.

match_question_text: The unpolluted natural rain water is slightly acidic due to the reaction of rain water with:

set.explanation_long: CO₂ present naturally in the atmosphere dissolves into falling raindrops, reacting as CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid), a weak acid that lowers rainwater's pH to around 5.6 even without any pollution. Additional pollutants (like sulfur/nitrogen oxides) can make rain considerably MORE acidic (true 'acid rain'), but the baseline natural acidity comes from dissolved CO₂. (The printed UHS key marks A, sulphur dioxide, but SO₂ causes polluted acid rain; the natural slight acidity of clean rain (pH ≈ 5.6) comes from dissolved CO₂, so C is used.)

match_question_text: In comparison with oxygen gas, a strong triple bond is present between two nitrogen atoms in a molecule and therefore nitrogen gas is:

set.explanation_short: The very strong N≡N triple bond makes nitrogen a very unreactive gas — but not completely inert, since it does react under suitable conditions.
set.explanation_long: Breaking the N≡N triple bond needs 946 kJ mol⁻¹, so nitrogen reacts far less readily than oxygen. It is not completely inert like the noble gases, however: it combines with hydrogen in the Haber process, with oxygen during lightning, and with hot metals such as magnesium and lithium to form nitrides. 'Very less reactive' is therefore the accurate description. (The printed UHS key marks B, but nitrogen does form compounds, so it is not completely inert.)
set.explanation_trick: N₂ is unreactive, not inert — think of the Haber process and nitrides of Mg and Li.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — the strong triple bond makes nitrogen unreactive, not highly reactive.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — unlike the noble gases, nitrogen forms compounds such as NH₃, NO and Mg₃N₂.
explanation_options.c: Correct — nitrogen is a very unreactive gas because of its strong triple bond.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — nitrogen is much less reactive than 'moderately reactive' suggests.

Newly produced cells/individuals which are identical in each other are known as

set.explanation_short: Genetically identical cells or individuals produced from a single parent are called clones.
set.explanation_long: A clone is a group of cells or organisms that are genetically identical because they arise from one ancestor by asexual reproduction, cell division or cloning techniques. Genetically modified and transgenic organisms, by contrast, have had their DNA deliberately altered, often with a gene from another species; they are not defined by being identical to one another. (The printed UHS key marks A, but 'genetically modified' does not mean identical, so D is used.)
set.explanation_trick: Identical copies = clones; altered DNA = genetically modified / transgenic.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — genetically modified organisms have altered DNA; they are not defined as identical copies.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — transgenic animals carry a foreign gene; that is not the same as being identical.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — transgenic bacteria carry foreign genes; that is not the same as being identical.
explanation_options.d: Correct — genetically identical cells or individuals are clones.

match_question_text: Oxidative phosphorylation, synthesis of ATP in the presence of oxygen occurs in:

set.explanation_short: Oxidative phosphorylation — making ATP using the electron transport chain with oxygen as the final acceptor — occurs in all aerobic cells.
set.explanation_long: In oxidative phosphorylation, electrons from NADH and FADH₂ pass along the electron transport chain to oxygen, and the energy released drives ATP synthase. Because oxygen is essential, the process occurs in all aerobic cells — in the mitochondria of eukaryotes and at the cell membrane of aerobic bacteria. Anaerobic cells cannot carry it out. (The printed UHS key marks C, 'all primitive cells', which is not a meaningful category for this oxygen-dependent process.)
set.explanation_trick: Oxidative phosphorylation needs oxygen, so it happens wherever respiration is aerobic.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — anaerobic cells cannot carry out oxidative phosphorylation.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — anaerobic cells, by definition, do not use oxygen.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — 'primitive cells' is not a category defined by oxidative phosphorylation; many primitive cells are anaerobic.
explanation_options.d: Correct — oxidative phosphorylation occurs in all aerobic cells.
